paragraphs: This week I practice for the school fun run. The fun run is on Saturday, the twenty-first of November. On Monday, the sixteenth, I run in the park with Tom. Tom is eleven, and I am ten. I am quick, but Tom is quicker. On Tuesday, the seventeenth, it rains all day. The road is wet, so it is dangerous. My mom says, "You must be at home today." I do my homework, and then I read a comic.

On Wednesday, the eighteenth, the sun comes out. The road is dry. When school ends, I run for twenty minutes. My legs are tired, but they are strong. I drink a lot of water. My shoes are old, but they are good. On Thursday, the nineteenth, Ben says, "Run with me." We run around the school field. Ben is slow today, and I wait for him. On Friday, the twentieth, I go to bed at eight o'clock. I am asleep very quickly.

On Saturday, the twenty-first, I wake up at six o'clock. The sky is blue, and the air is cool. Is it the big day? Yes, it is! My dad takes me to school at seven o'clock. Many children are on the field. The run starts at eight o'clock. Tom and Ben run next to me. I am not first, and I am not last. My mom and dad clap at the end. I am very tired, but I am very happy.
